sources.title: Historical atlas: Kingdom of Kapisa, 700 to 800
sources.note: Exact indexed record kingdom-of-kapisa, 700 to 800, circa. One decoded feature has bounds 67.189,31.744,73.191,36.520. Atlas metadata is not an independently verified ancient frontier. See identities.json.

sources.title: Xavier de Planhol, Kabul II: Historical Geography, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct full scholarly article, Location and Early History; The urbanization of the basin: from Kapisa to Kabul. Used for topography, political centers and broad Turk Shahi identity, not its older circa-850 succession date. The newer Verdon study supplies the qualified circa-822 ending.

sources.title: Noémie Verdon, Titles, Cultural History, and Chronology of the Shahi Kings (2026)
sources.note: Direct scholarly publication from the Austrian Science Fund Shahi project, chapter 1. Literary Sources and Updated Tentative Chronology: 738/739 accession, 745 successor, circa-822 transition, not an exact accession day. Introductory religious-identity discussion rejects instant religious replacement. Conservatively grouped with chapters 4 and 7 as one publication work for the 200-word budget.

sources.title: Ehsan Shavarebi and Arturo Annucci, Coin Finds of the Shahi Kingdoms in the Indo-Iranian Borderlands (2026)
sources.note: Direct research publication, chapter 4, find complex 4 Fondukistan: clay urn under royal-couple statues, three Shri Shahi coins plus Khosrow II coin from 627/28 with circa-689 countermarks. Later mark supplies earliest possible deposit date, not precise construction date. Same publication work as Verdon and Qol-e Tut chapters.

sources.title: Michael Alram, Arturo Annucci and Nikolaus Schindel, Qol-e Tut: A Catalogue of Coins (2026)
sources.note: Direct numismatic research, chapter 7. Introduction: site used roughly sixth through eleventh centuries. Numismatic-historical commentary around notes 81 to 83 contrasts local drachms/aes with higher-silver Sasanian/Arab coins for supra-regional transactions. Same publication work as chapters 1 and 4.

sources.title: Hyecho, Memoir of a Pilgrimage to the Five Regions of India, Taisho 2089, National Central University text
sources.note: Primary Chinese text, CBETA edition revised 2005, issued 2006, university-hosted PDF. Direct fetch failed; full institutional indexed PDF page 5 read with query 罽賓國冬天積雪 土地出駝. Kapisa passage: seasonal royal residence, shirts/trousers/boots, crops, families supporting monasteries. Textile die can mean cotton/fine wool; public copy does not insist on one fiber. Hyecho journey account belongs to the 720s; no exact date of individual observations asserted. Modern Chinese transcription, not original manuscript image.

sources.title: Mónica López-Prat and colleagues, The modeling pastes of monumental terracruda sculpture (2024)
sources.note: Original Archaeometry paper, online 2023, volume 66 (2024), 76 to 99. Full publisher indexed text read; direct publisher returned 403 and Barcelona PDF extraction empty. Introduction gives wood/clay/stucco technique and sites spanning fifth to eleventh centuries. Results Pigments characterization gives QT1 lazurite/hematite and QT2 pink hematite; Methods Petrography says toe QT4 was not thin-sectioned. All university mirrors and Zenodo data grouped as one work; no exact eighth-century attribution for undated rubble samples.

sources.title: Zafar Paiman, The Buddhist monastery of Tepe Narenj in the light of recent excavations, SEECHAC
sources.note: Direct excavator conference summary: circular chapel caption explicitly eighth century, sixteen bodhisattvas on circular bench; broader site fifth/sixth to late tenth century from pottery and coins. No identification of ancient site name from later local name.

sources.title: Musée Guimet, Divinity seated in a royal-ease position, MG 18959
sources.note: Direct museum collection entry: seventh-century clay figure, 72 x 24 x 22 cm, Fondukistan, Jean Carl mission 1937. Courtyard, small central stupa, painted/sculpted niches and mirrored arrangement. Museum dates this object to seventh century; public copy labels it an earlier example rather than inventing an eighth-century manufacture date.

sources.title: Kunsthistorisches Museum, Tegin Chorasan Shah coin, GR 43746
sources.note: Full museum indexed original checked; direct web fetch failed. Catalogue dates circa 680 to 740, non-ferrous metal, 0.73 g, diameter 13.9 mm, mint Kabulistan or Gandhara. Beschriftung gives Bactrian (verderbt) ταγινo Þαυo and German translation Tegin, der König. Public Latin transliteration tagino šauo follows this reading; irregular legend remains qualified. No reconstructed ancient glyph image. Museum accession 2019 is not coin manufacture or excavation date.

proposedOverrides.name: Kapisa and the early Kabul Shahis
proposedOverrides.summary: An eighth-century Shahi crossroads linking Kapisa, Kabul and Gandhara, with varied communities and older cultural foundations.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One exact indexed record; no aliases or shared narrative.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Earlier Kushan and Hunnic histories do not become this dynasty. Modern Kapisa Province is not identical to ancient Kapisa or the atlas polygon. Turk Shahi is a conventional dynastic label, not an assertion of homogeneous population or exclusive religion. Traveler accounts and seventh-century archaeological background are explicitly dated. New 2026 chronology qualifies transition around 822, avoiding Iranica’s older 850 date. No invented hospital, toilet, recipe or school-attendance statistics. Bactrian writing uses museum-supported transliteration because glyph-level reading is irregular. No successor link: Hindu Shahis indexed geometry begins 900, after circa-822 transition.
